chunks: He was asked, 'How many times should the man pour upon his hand before he enters it into the vessel?' He said: 'Once for the ritual impurity of urine, twice for faeces, and three times for sexual impurity (janaba).'

key_terms.الْإِنَاء: Vessel — a container of water used for ritual purification (wudu or ghusl)
key_terms.الْجَنَابَة: Janaba — major ritual impurity resulting from sexual intercourse or seminal discharge, requiring full ghusl
key_terms.حَدَث: Hadath — ritual impurity, a state requiring purification before worship

ai.seo_question: How many times should one wash hands before putting them in a vessel for wudu or ghusl?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) specifies the number of times water must be poured over the hands before dipping them into a vessel: once for urine, twice for faeces, and three times for janaba (major ritual impurity). This ruling addresses the concern of contaminating the water used for purification, a fundamental principle in Shia jurisprudence. The three-tiered response reflects the varying severity of ritual impurity, with janaba — the major impurity requiring full ghusl — demanding the most thorough pre-rinse.
